stem: Who was the first ruler of the Khilji dynasty?
expl: Jalaluddin Khilji founded the Khilji dynasty in 1290 A.D. He had his coronation in 1290 A.D. in the unfinished Kilokhari (Kilughari) palace built by Kaiqubad. According to Dr. A.L. Srivastava, Jalaluddin Khilji was the first Turkish Sultan of Delhi who placed before himself the principle of “liberal despotism.”

stem: "Thus to Ala-ud-din belongs the credit of being the first Turkish Sultan of Delhi to bring the church under the control of the state and to usher in factors that might make the state secular in theory." Who wrote these words?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A.L. Srivastava, in his book The Sultanate of Delhi (711– 1526 A.D.), wrote about Alauddin Khilji: “Alauddin was the first Turkish Sultan of Delhi who was credited with bringing religion under the control of the state and introducing such elements which, in theory, made the state secular.”

stem: “When he attained Kingship, he was fully independent of rules and orders of Shariat.” For which Sultan Barani made this statement?
expl: Ziauddin Barani made the above statement for Alauddin Khalji. Alauddin was the first Sultan of Delhi who established state control over religion. Explaining his policy in this context, he himself said that, “I do not know what is right and what is wrong in the eyes of the law. I give orders for whatever I consider suitable for the welfare of the state or for a particular occasion. What will happen to me on the Day of Judgment, I do not know.” Alauddin revived Balban’s idea regarding kingship. He believed in the sovereign authority of the king, who is merely the representative of God on earth. He did not consider it necessary to seek the Caliph’s permission to increase his power; therefore, he made no request to the Caliph for recognition of his position. He described himself as ‘Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir Amir-ul-Muminin’. Thus, Alauddin was the first Sultan of Delhi who did not allow religion to interfere in politics. Alauddin remained free from the influence of the ulama.

stem: Who among the army-commanders of Alauddin Khilji died fighting against the Mongols?
expl: Alauddin’s famous general Zafar Khan was killed while fighting the Mongols. He was the best and bravest general of his time.

stem: Padmini is associated with Ala-ud-Din’s conquest of Chittor. She was the wife of
expl: The story of Padmini is based on the poetic work ‘Padmavat’, written in 1540 AD by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. According to it, Padmini was the extremely beautiful and learned wife of Rana Ratan Singh of Chittor. Amir Khusro mentioned the love episode of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba in his work, and in his hints he compared Alauddin to Solomon and Padmini to Sheba. Probably on this basis, Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat, and the story of Queen Padmini as the queen of Rana Ratan Singh took shape.

stem: Who was the ruler of Chittor at the time of Alauddin Khilji’s invasion?
expl: The story of Padmini is based on the poetic work ‘Padmavat’, written in 1540 AD by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. Probably on this basis, Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat, and the story of Queen Padmini as the queen of Rana Ratan Singh took shape.

stem: Who was the ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin Khilji’s invasion?
expl: At the time of Alauddin Khilji’s invasion, Ramchandra Dev was the Yadava dynasty ruler of Devagiri. During Jalaluddin Khilji’s reign, Alauddin Khalji first attacked Devagiri in 1296 AD and forced its ruler Ramchandra Dev to pay an annual tribute. But after Alauddin became the Sultan, when Ramchandra Dev stopped paying the annual tribute, Alauddin, angered by this, sent an army against Devagiri under the leadership of Malik Kafur. In this war, Ramchandra Dev was defeated and he surrendered.

stem: During the regime of which Sultan was the Khalisa land developed on a large scale?
expl: The main objective of Alauddin’s revenue and land-tax system was to establish a powerful and autocratic state. He confiscated land from those persons who had received it as milk-idrar, inam, and waqf (land received as a religious/ charitable endowment), etc. As a result, Khalisa land was developed on a large scale.

stem: Which Sultan demanded half the crops on land after measurement as revenue?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to introduce certain changes in land-revenue policy. He fixed 50% of the produce as land revenue and insisted that it should be collected in the form of grain. Before him, Balban and Iltutmish did not levy land revenue at a rate higher than one-third of the produce. During the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq too, the rate of land tax was 50%, similar to Alauddin’s. Although in this question both options (c) and (d) are correct, the Bihar Public Service Commission, in its final answer key, accepted option (c) as correct.

stem: Who was deputed for the conquest of Dwarasamudra by Ala-ud-din Khilji ?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Alauddin Khilji appointed Malik Kafur for the conquest of Dwarasamudra. Dwarasamudra was the capital of the Hoysala kingdom, and its ruler was Vira Ballala III. The conquest of most parts of South India is largely credited to Malik Kafur.

stem: Nizamuddin Auliya refused to meet which Sultan?
expl: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya witnessed the reign of more than seven Sultans who came to power one after another; however, he never went to anyone’s court. Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji was probably the first ruler who, after hearing about the Shaikh’s fame and greatness, offered him a few villages and expressed a desire to meet him. The Shaikh refused, saying: “My khanqah has two doors; if the Sultan enters from one, I will leave from the other.” Later, when Sultan Jalaluddin wished to meet him without prior notice, Auliya’s beloved disciple Amir Khusro informed Auliya about it. As soon as he received the information, Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya immediately left for Ajodhan to visit his spiritual master (Baba Farid). Thus, Auliya continued to avoid meeting the Sultan directly. It is also mentioned that Alauddin Khilji wished to meet Auliya, but no such dramatic incident is associated with Alauddin as is associated with Jalaluddin.

stem: Who started the Public Distribution System in the Sultanate period?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khilji started the Public Distribution System

stem: Malik Kafur also known as "Hazar Dinari" was bought by whom ?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the famous book 'History of Khalijis' written by famous historian K.S.Lal, around 1299 CE, during Alauddin Khilji’s Gujarat campaign, the commander Nusrat Khan attacked the wealthy port of Cambay (Khambhat) and obtained a large amount of gold, silver, jewels, and other valuable items. During the same campaign, the slave Malik Kafur was captured. This was the time when Nusrat Khan seized Malik Kafur from his owner. Since Malik Kafur’s owner had purchased him for one thousand dinars, he came to be called “Hazar-Dinari.” Along with the booty, Nusrat Khan sent Malik Kafur to Delhi to Alauddin. Later, impressed by Kafur’s extraordinary ability and personality, Sultan Alauddin Khilji made him his most trusted commander. The credit for Alauddin’s Deccan campaigns and victories is mainly given to Malik Kafur. From this description, it is clear that Nusrat Khan did not purchase Malik Kafur; rather, he captured him during the Gujarat campaign. Therefore, the closest answer is option (c).

stem: Who among the following opposed the power of the Khalifa?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: None of the sultans given in the options opposed the power of the Khalifa. Iltutmish obtained recognition from the Khalifa; however, the Sultan of Bengal, Ghiyasuddin, had also obtained recognition from the Khalifa. By attacking him, Iltutmish, in a way, also challenged the authority of the Khalifa. Alauddin Khilji, Balban, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq were all practically independent rulers, but none of them opposed the power or authority of the Khalifa. Only Mubarak Khilji declared himself the Khalifa and assumed the title Khalifatullah. In this way, he opposed the authority of the Khalifa.

stem: Who among the following rulers, ruled for the maximum period?
expl: The reigns of these four rulers of the Delhi Sultanate are estimated to be as follows: Alauddin Khilji – approximately 20 years. Muhammad bin Tughlaq – approximately 26 years. Ghiyasuddin Balban – approximately 20/21 years. Bahlol Lodi, the founder of the Lodi dynasty, reigned approximately 38 years, which is clearly longer than all the other rulers mentioned above.

stem: Which one of the following Sultans provided employment to the unemployed?
expl: Firoz Shah Tughlaq carried out some welfare works for the benefit of ordinary people. He opened an office for appointments (employment office) and, after thoroughly examining each person’s qualities and abilities, he appointed as many people as possible and tried to solve the problem of unemployment.

stem: Which of the following Sultan had the most number of slaves in his court?
expl: Firoz Tughlaq was very fond of slaves. During his time, the number of slaves possibly reached up to 180,000. For their supervision, a separate department (Diwan-i-Bandagan) was formed, and full attention was given to the education of the slaves.

stem: What was ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ established by Firoz Tughluq?
expl: Firoz Tughlaq was the first Indian ruler who arranged Hajj at the expense of the state. He also established a charitable hospital named Dar-ul-Shafa (also written Dar-ul-Shifa) and appointed skilled physicians (hakims) there.

stem: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi introduced measures for improving the quality of fruits?
expl: Due to his interest in horticulture, Firoz Shah Tughlaq got about 1200 new gardens planted near Delhi, and he also took measures to improve the quality of fruits in those gardens.

stem: Which Delhi Sultan built the maximum number of canals?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq became famous for creating the largest network of canals in India. To provide irrigation facilities, he constructed five major canals. After obtaining the approval of the ulema (religious scholars), Firoz Tughlaq was the first Delhi Sultan to impose an irrigation tax called Haqq-e-Sharb. Farmers who used water from royal canals for irrigation had to pay an additional tax equal to one-tenth of their produce.

stem: Which one of the following dynasties ruled over India after the invasion of Timur?
expl: Timur’s invasion (1398 AD) greatly weakened the Delhi Sultanate and the power of the Tughlaq dynasty, and it hastened their decline. With the death of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah in 1412 AD, the Tughlaq dynasty came to an end. In 1413 AD, the nobles chose Daulat Khan as the Sultan of Delhi; however, he was defeated by Khizr Khan. Khizr Khan was the Subahdar (provincial governor) of Multan appointed by Timur. Later, he captured Lahore, Dipalpur, and Upper Sindh. After Timur’s invasion, in 1414 AD, he took control of Delhi and laid the foundation of a new dynasty—the Sayyid dynasty.

stem: Which of the following Sultans founded a town where now stands Agra?
expl: In 1504 AD, Sikandar Lodi founded a new city named Agra on the banks of the Yamuna River with the objective of keeping the rulers of Rajasthan under control, and he made it his capital. He made efforts to promote agriculture and trade. A standard measure called “Gaz-e-Sikandari” was introduced during his time. He arranged free food for the poor. During his reign, a list of capable persons was prepared and presented before him every six months. He was educated and scholarly. On his orders, an Ayurvedic text was translated into Persian and was named “Farhang-e-Sikandari.” During his period, an excellent treatise on vocal music, “Lazzat-e-Sikandarshahi,” was composed. Sikandar Lodi was very fond of listening to the shehnai. He wrote poems under the pen-name “Gulrukhi.”

stem: Who was the founder of the Vijayanagara Empire?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 AD during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq by two brothers, Harihara and Bukka. The capital of this kingdom was Hampi, situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

stem: Identify the first ruler of Vijayanagara who captured Goa from the Bahamani’s?
expl: After Bukka’s death in 1377 AD, his son Harihara II (1377– 1404 AD) ascended the throne and adopted the title “Maharajadhiraja.” He conquered regions like Kanara, Mysore, Tiruchanapalli, Kanchi, etc., and collected tribute from the king of Sri Lanka. He also struggled with the Bahmani kingdom. Harihara II’s greatest achievement was the capture of Goa in the west from the Bahmani state. He was a devotee of Shiva (in the form of Virupaksha).

stem: With whom did the king of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya fought the battle of Golconda?
expl: Vijayanagara king Krishnadeva Raya fought the Golconda war against the Golconda Sultan Quli Qutb Shah. The Qutb Shahi dynasty in Golconda was founded by Quli Qutb Shah. When Krishnadeva Raya was busy in a war with Odisha, Qutb Shah attacked the forts of Pangala and Guntur located on the Vijayanagar frontier and captured forts such as Warangal, Kondavidu, etc. After this, he tried to attack Vijayanagar. A conflict took place between Krishnadeva Raya and Qutb Shah, and the Qutb Shahi army was defeated.

stem: What was the chief characteristic of the financial system of the Vijayanagara Empire?
expl: The Vijayanagara state derived income from various sources, such as land revenue, property tax, trade tax, professional tax, taxes imposed on industries, social and community taxes, and fines imposed for crimes. Land was properly surveyed, and 1/6 of the produce was collected as land tax (1/6 as land tax was the ideal rate, but in practice it ranged between 1/6 and 1/3 depending on the productivity of the land). A tax called ‘Shisht’ (land tax) was the chief source of the state’s income. The central revenue department was called ‘Athavane’ (Asthavan or Athvan).

stem: The remains of the Vijayanagara Empire are found in?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: The ruins of Hampi (located in present-day Karnataka) represent the ancient capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. The famous Virupaksha Temple is located here. Hampi is also included in the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list.

stem: Which among the following King's region Persian traveller 'Abdur Razzaq' came to India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Persian ambassador Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya II of the Sangama dynasty (tenure: 1422–1446 A.D.).

stem: Who among the following famous rulers founded a suburban township of Nagalapuram, near Vijayanagara, after his mother's name?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 A.D.) was a ruler of the Tuluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire and is considered its most powerful ruler. He founded Nagalambapuram, now known as Nagalapuram, named after his mother Nagalamba. It is located in the Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh.

stem: Which famous war took place in 1565 A.D.?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In 1565, in the famous Battle of Talikota, the combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, and Bidar defeated Vijayanagara. In this combined army, Berar alone was not included. According to Firishta, the battle was fought at Talikota, but the actual battlefield lay between two villages named Rakkasi and Tangadi. At the time of the Battle of Talikota, Sadasiva Raya was the ruler of Vijayanagara, but the real power was in the hands of his minister Rama Raya. Rama Raya was a capable commander; he tried to create divisions among the Muslim rulers of the Bahmani states, but he did not succeed. In this very battle, Hussain Nizam Shah personally killed Rama Raya.
